entries.text: Thank you for calling VeloFit. Your call may be recorded for quality assurance. Please wait while I connect you to the next available agent.
Thank you for holding. My name is David, agent ID 304. How can I help you today?
Finally! I've been on hold forever. My name is Sarah Miller, and this VeloBand you sold me is a piece of junk.

I'm very sorry to hear you're having trouble, Sarah. I can pull up your account with the phone number you're calling from. One moment... Okay, I see your recent purchase of the VeloBand GPS Tracker. To make sure I understand, what specifically is the issue? Is it a technical fault or a preference?

A fault? It's completely broken! The heart rate monitor is not working at all, and the whole thing won't sync with my phone. I've tried everything. This thing is defective and I want my money back. Now.
I certainly understand your frustration. When a device isn't syncing or tracking properly, it can be very disruptive. I see you received the band on December 15th, about 22 days ago.
I don't care what day it is! Are you going to give me a refund or do I need to speak to your manager? I'm not going to be ignored on this. I'll post a review on every website you can think of.
That won't be necessary, Sarah. Please give me just one moment to check our policy for you... Okay, I've just reviewed it. You are well within our 90-day return window.
So you'll process the refund? No more games?

Yes, absolutely. Since the item is defective and you're within the timeframe, I can approve that for you right now. I'm generating a prepaid return shipping label that I'll email to you. Once we receive the device, you'll see a full refund to your original payment method within 3-5 business days.
Okay. Good. That's all I wanted in the first place. Just send the email.
I've just sent it. The email is on its way to S-Miller at G-mail dot com. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?
Thank you for calling VeloFit. Have a good day.
